```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
library(readfiscalau)
```

The historical-table snapshot makes persistent economic forecasts, fiscal
projections, reconciliations, debt and interest tables, and formal financial
statements available without reparsing PDFs during a user query. It is a
static RDS installed with the package and built from 53 official Treasury
publications:

- 28 Budgets from 2000–01 through 2026–27, including the March and October
  2022–23 Budgets; and
- 25 MYEFOs from 2000–01 through 2025–26. No 2022–23 MYEFO was issued.

Values reproduce the cells printed in the named publication vintage. They are
not silently revised into a latest-actual series. Every table retains its
published title, page, official URL, and PDF SHA-256.

## What is included

The catalogue is the source of truth for family-level coverage. `query_mode`
has three meanings:

- `series_and_table`: durable dated rows are queryable as canonical series,
  and the complete parsed table is also available;
- `hybrid`: durable headline rows are series while variable reconciliation
  detail remains available through the complete-table reader; and
- `table_only`: the complete table is the public contract, without promising
  stable component-row identities.

```{r family-coverage}
families <- list_au_budget_myefo_families()
knitr::kable(families[, c(
  "family_label", "query_mode",
  "budget_first_vintage", "budget_last_vintage", "budget_release_count",
  "myefo_first_vintage", "myefo_last_vintage", "myefo_release_count"
)])
```

These are table-discovery dates, not universal series envelopes. A family may
contain earlier actual periods and later forecasts; individual rows can begin
later, and missing publications or material presentation changes remain
visible in the counts. Start with `list_au_budget_myefo_series()` when raw
source-cell coverage matters. Use `list_au_budget_myefo_actual_histories()`
for one package-constructed actual path across publications, and
`list_au_budget_myefo_series_profiles()` for exact release-specific forecast
paths. Their direct readers return chart-ready series without application-side
assembly.

The selected families focus on:

- major economic parameters, international GDP forecasts, and detailed
  domestic forecasts;
- GGS Budget, accrual and balance-sheet aggregates, underlying/headline cash
  balances, fiscal-balance reconciliations, and formal sector statements;
- detailed cash receipts, tax-receipt parameters, and cash/accrual
  reconciliations;
- expense estimates, function/sub-function expenses, and net capital
  investment;
- forecast AGS, net debt, and cash/accrual interest.

Source charts, department-specific appendices, appropriation detail, and the
many program tables at the ends of Budget documents are outside this snapshot.

## Query a durable row across publications

One economic or fiscal concept has one canonical `series_id`, even if it is
printed in several tables. The example below reads the preferred underlying
cash-balance occurrence from the 2026–27 Budget bridge table.

```{r canonical-series}
ucb <- read_au_budget_myefo_series(
  "underlying-cash-balance",
  release = "treasury-budget-2026-27-final",
  unit = "AUD million"
)
ucb[, c(
  "budget_vintage", "fiscal_year", "value", "unit",
  "actual_forecast", "profile_type", "source_table"
)]
```

`all_sources = FALSE` is the default. It keeps one preferred occurrence per
release, period, unit, accounting basis, and publication profile. Use
`all_sources = TRUE` to inspect the same canonical concept wherever it appears
in aggregate, reconciliation, bridge, or formal-statement tables.

```{r duplicate-sources}
ucb_sources <- read_au_budget_myefo_series(
  "underlying-cash-balance",
  release = "treasury-budget-2026-27-final",
  unit = "AUD million",
  all_sources = TRUE
)
unique(ucb_sources[, c("series_id", "family_id", "source_table")])
```

This prevents a Table 3.3 underlying cash balance and a Table 3.5 underlying
cash balance from becoming separate user-facing series. Budget and MYEFO
profiles are not deduplicated into one forecast: `profile_type` keeps a prior
Budget estimate, an updated MYEFO estimate, and actual/outcome columns distinct.

## Query every durable row from a detailed forecast table

The detailed domestic-economy family exposes all durable rows rather than only
a small headline subset. In the 2026–27 Budget, this is 23 rows, including GDP,
consumption, investment, demand, trade, prices, wages, labour-market measures,
the current account, and net overseas migration.

```{r domestic-table}
domestic <- read_au_budget_myefo_table(
  "treasury-budget-2026-27-final",
  "domestic_economy_detailed_forecasts"
)
domestic_series <- unique(domestic[
  domestic$series_eligible,
  c("series_id", "series", "row_path", "unit")
])
nrow(domestic_series)
head(domestic_series, 8)
```

Select one row with its canonical ID:

```{r mining-investment}
mining <- domestic[
  domestic$series_id == "mining-investment" & domestic$series_eligible,
  c("fiscal_year", "period_end", "value", "unit", "actual_forecast")
]
mining
```

The detailed cash-receipts family uses the same model. All 37 categories in
the 2026–27 Budget Table 5.7 are queryable, and `row_path` retains headings
such as the excise-and-customs hierarchy.

```{r receipts-table}
receipts <- read_au_budget_myefo_table(
  "treasury-budget-2026-27-final",
  "detailed_cash_receipts"
)
receipt_series <- unique(receipts[
  receipts$series_eligible,
  c("series_id", "series", "row_path", "unit")
])
nrow(receipt_series)
receipt_series[receipt_series$series_id %in% c(
  "company-tax", "goods-and-services-tax", "petrol", "total-receipts"
), ]
```

## Read a complete variable table

Reconciliation components often change with policy decisions, asset sales,
programs, and presentation. `read_au_budget_myefo_table()` therefore returns
every parsed numeric cell, including non-time `Total` columns and rows that are
not series-queryable.

```{r full-bridge}
bridge <- read_au_budget_myefo_table(
  "treasury-budget-2026-27-final",
  "underlying_to_headline_cash_bridge"
)
bridge[1:8, c(
  "row_path", "column_label", "value", "unit", "series_eligible"
)]
```

`format = "text"` returns the layout-preserving extracted text for each
physical table part. This is useful for footnotes and variable row context.
The expense-estimate reconciliation (often Table 3.13 in recent Budgets) is
deliberately table-only.

```{r table-only}
expense <- read_au_budget_myefo_table(
  "treasury-budget-2026-27-final",
  "expense_estimates_reconciliation",
  format = "text"
)
expense[, c(
  "budget_vintage", "source_table", "source_page",
  "source_url", "source_sha256"
)]
```

## Interpretation and provenance

The parser normalizes printed numbers—including historical mixed fractions—to
numeric `value`, but retains `value_text`, `raw_line`, and complete `raw_text`.
`unit_multiplier` converts the displayed unit to base units when required.
Non-time totals have no `period_end` and are never canonical series.

Accounting bases, government-sector scopes, row definitions, and forecast
horizons can change between vintages. Use `accounting_basis`, `consolidation`,
`actual_forecast`, `profile_type`, `source_table`, and `source_page` when making
comparisons; inspect the source footnotes for material definition changes.
The reader does not claim a continuous accounting concept merely because a
canonical label persists.

The installed reader performs no network request, PDF parsing, cache write, or
working-directory write. A maintainer rebuild requires the frozen official PDF
inventory and layout-preserving text extraction; the generated RDS records the
53 source URLs and PDF hashes used for verification.
